pitches.logline: Poppy talks in her sleep at 3am and says the wrong name. Élodie is awake, uncharmed, and taking notes. By breakfast two women want the same Brazilian, one attacks it with insults, one attacks it with elegant nothing, and Lucas hugs them both inside ninety seconds because he genuinely likes everyone — which is the most dangerous thing anyone in this villa has ever done. Meanwhile Brock has mistaken 'thank you for the water' for a merger, Matteo is cooking lasagne for eleven people who did not ask, and at sunset the gate opens on a man holding one red carnation and no explanation. The reversal isn't that Élodie wants Lucas. It's that she already had him, on day two, for two minutes, in silence — and that changes what Poppy's sleeping voice was actually confessing.
pitches.want: Poppy wants to want nobody; Élodie wants to be wanted without moving; Lucas wants everyone warm and no one hurt; Brock wants a five-year plan by lunch.
pitches.lieOrSecret: Élodie kissed Lucas on day two and told no one — not even Lucas, who has been treating it as a friendly accident. Poppy's poetry notebook under the mattress already rhymes 'Lucas' with 'ruckus'. Twice.
pitches.publicCollision: Truth-or-dare by the fire pit: Sienna dares Élodie to rate every man out of ten. She says 'Lucas — a five.' Lucas laughs, wounded. Poppy defends him too fast, too loud, in front of Matteo, who is holding a lasagne. The lasagne goes down on the table like a gavel.
pitches.reversal: Élodie mentions the day-two kiss to shut Poppy up — and the audience instantly re-sees the 3am sleep-talk: Poppy wasn't dreaming about Lucas, she was dreaming about the kiss she half-saw from the balcony and told herself she imagined. She's been jealous for four days without permission to be. Her 'insult everyone' armour was built that night. On camera. We watched her build it and thought it was a personality.
pitches.whyItsFunny: Four people running four incompatible operating systems at the same emotional event: Brock proposing to a glass of water, Matteo weaponising carbohydrates against a threat he can't name, Élodie rating a man a five with her whole face saying nine, and Poppy defending him so hard she indicts herself.

pitches.logline: Rohan's compatibility algorithm predicts the villa's four couples with unsettling accuracy, so everyone starts obeying it — until it spits out a pairing that ruins Poppy's entire night's work. Poppy sleep-said a name at 3am; Élodie heard it; Rohan's spreadsheet independently produced the same name at 9am and read it aloud at breakfast like a weather report. Now two women are at war over a Brazilian who thinks the tension is about swimming, Greta has scheduled the war for 19:00–19:30, and Brock is pitching everyone equity in a lemonade company. Then the gate opens and the algorithm has no row for him.
pitches.want: Rohan wants to be right before he's brave; Poppy wants deniability; Élodie wants the result without the effort; Lucas wants no one to notice he never goes past the pool steps.
pitches.lieOrSecret: The algorithm is astrology in a spreadsheet with a lanyard on. Rohan knows. He also knows Élodie kissed Lucas on day two, because she asked him to 'not put that in the data'.
pitches.publicCollision: Rohan reads compatibility scores aloud to prove his worth to Greta. Poppy–Lucas: 94. Élodie–Lucas: 96. Élodie says 'he is a five' with total serenity. Greta demands the methodology. Rohan produces a birth chart. The villa turns on him for ninety glorious seconds and it saves Poppy's dignity by accident.
pitches.reversal: Rohan didn't calculate anything. Élodie fed him the numbers days ago to smoke Poppy out without ever having to speak first — meaning Élodie's famous 'do nothing' isn't laziness, it's the most active campaign in the villa, and every previous scene where she sat beautifully doing nothing was a move.
pitches.whyItsFunny: A man defending astrology like it's peer-reviewed while the woman who forged his data sunbathes six feet away, and Brock trying to invest in the algorithm.

pitches.logline: Matteo makes lasagne for eleven because he can feel a betrayal coming, and he is right — he's just wrong about which one. While he cooks, Poppy sleep-says a Brazilian's name, Élodie hears it and rates the moment a six, and a two-minute kiss from day two starts leaking out of the walls. By sunset Matteo has fed everyone who is about to hurt him, Brock has proposed a joint venture to a woman who thanked him for water, and a stranger with a red carnation walks through the gate mid-toast. Nobody eats the lasagne. Matteo notices. Matteo will remember.
pitches.want: Matteo wants to be chosen for his devotion; Poppy wants to deny everything including footage; Élodie wants to win without competing; Brock wants a headline.
pitches.lieOrSecret: Matteo is lactose intolerant and has been suffering nightly for a mozzarella persona he invented. The lasagne is literally killing him. Also: Poppy has never once said his name in her sleep, and she knows it.
pitches.publicCollision: The dinner. Matteo toasts 'loyalty'. Poppy can't say it back fast enough. Lucas hugs both women in the same minute, oblivious. Élodie says 'Lucas is a five.' Matteo puts down the serving spoon very, very gently.
pitches.reversal: Matteo didn't sense anything. He heard Poppy sleep-talk too — he was awake before Élodie was — and the eight-course apology dinner was a bribe to a woman who hadn't chosen yet. So his grand romantic gesture re-reads as panic, and his 'seduction' was a man begging quietly in four courses.
pitches.whyItsFunny: A man poisoning himself with cheese to seem romantic, at a table where nobody is loyal, delivering a loyalty toast.

whyChosen: It's the only pitch where the reversal rewrites the episode's very first image — the 3am sleep-talk — so a cold viewer immediately re-watches minute one in their head, which is the strongest possible hook for Episode 2. It centres the four focus characters without needing setup, gives every nation an equally absurd flaw (Brock's over-commitment, Poppy's armour, Élodie's stillness, Matteo's carbohydrates, Lucas's warmth), and every scene flips who's winning: Élodie wins the fire pit, loses it with the word 'five', regains it with the kiss reveal, and then loses everything when Alejandro's carnation makes her stillness look like standing still. It also leaves four live questions — the mattress, the pool steps, who Alejandro names, and whether Lucas knows anything at all — and Poppy's laugh that doesn't reach her eyes is a face-reaction beat you can still see when the credits roll.
